reading.text:
READING (locked before any Lean) -- spec:Dissertation.PaperSpec.A.sec4_uniq_homotopy
Reviewer: claude-auditor (same model family as the statements' author).

Passage (opening paragraph of subsection 4.4 "The continuation step", before Lemma 4.4):
"Taking identical sources and the common initial datum in Lemma 4.3 (at lower bound
lambda_ = lambda_*) yields uniqueness at each lambda in [lambda_*, 1]; Lemma 4.2 gives it on
[0, lambda_*]. It remains to prove existence up to lambda = 1."

Context: lambda_* is the small-coupling threshold of Lemma 4.2: lambda_* in (0,1] (in fact
(0,1/2]), depending only on T, L and c_BDG, with WP(lambda) for every lambda in [0, lambda_*]
under Assumptions 2.2-2.3. Lemma 4.3 (under Assumptions 2.3-2.5) bounds the difference of two
solutions of the forced system (4.1) at a parameter lambda in [lambda_, 1] by the data
differences, with constant C_B(T, L, ||G||, c_G, alpha, beta_1, beta_2, lambda_, c_BDG).
The subsection's Lemma 4.4 and the proof of Theorem 3.5 work under Assumptions 2.2-2.5.

"Uniqueness at lambda" = uniqueness part of WP(lambda): for every square-integrable forcing q
(q^b, q^sigma, q^f progressive, q^h predictable P x E-measurable, all square-integrable;
q^g_T in L^2(F_T)) and the given initial datum xi_0 in L^2(F_0), any two solutions Theta^1,
Theta^2 in H (S^2 x S^2 x H_W x H_N) of the forced system (4.1) at parameter lambda, with the
same q and xi_0, coincide in H (X, Y indistinguishable; Z equal dt x dP-a.e.; U equal
dt x dP x nu-a.e.; equivalently ||Theta^1 - Theta^2||_H = 0).

Faithful formal statement must contain:
 - Setting: the standing basis; coefficients b, sigma, h, f, g with the signatures of section 2
   (law argument the full-tuple law in P_2(H), h evaluated at the predictable tuple and mu^-);
   initial datum xi_0.
 - Hypotheses: Assumptions 2.2-2.5 (integrability at the origin, diagonal Lipschitz with L,
   full-rank G, terminal and interior expected diagonal G-monotonicity with alpha, beta_1, beta_2
   and the sign/rank conditions). [Uniqueness on [lambda_*,1] needs only 2.3-2.5, on [0,lambda_*]
   only 2.2-2.3; requiring 2.2-2.5 for both matches the hypotheses in force in the subsection.]
 - lambda_*: the threshold of Lemma 4.2 (depending only on T, L, c_BDG). Since [0,lambda_*] and
   [lambda_*,1] cover [0,1], the conclusion amounts to uniqueness at EVERY lambda in [0,1]; how
   lambda_* is quantified is then immaterial to the truth/strength of the conclusion, provided
   both pieces are stated for the same lambda_* in (0,1] (or the statement is simply for all
   lambda in [0,1]).
 - Conclusion: for every lambda in [lambda_*, 1] AND every lambda in [0, lambda_*], for every
   forcing q, any two H-solutions of (4.1) at lambda with forcing q and initial datum xi_0 are
   equal in H.
 - The notion "solution of (4.1)" must be the real one: both identities a.s. for every t in
   [0,T], with the Ito integral against W, the compensated Poisson integral against Ntilde, the
   law flows mu_t = Law(Theta_t), mu^-_t = Law(Theta^-_t) (Borel representatives), and h at the
   predictable tuple. Equality "in H" must be the equivalence of the solution space (not, say,
   equality of a weaker object).
 - Not required: existence (that is the next sentence, "It remains to prove existence").

comparison.text:
COMPARISON -- spec:Dissertation.PaperSpec.A.sec4_uniq_homotopy
Reviewer: claude-auditor (same model family as the statements' author).

Lean (PaperSpec/A/Sec4Continuation.lean:33-64): EXISTS lamStar : R -> R -> R such that for every
standing setting (LevyDriver D, G0 independent of the driver, filtration enlJoint, E countably
generated, nu sigma-finite), n, m, d >= 1, T > 0, constants L, alpha, beta1, beta2, G, coefficients
C, initial datum xi0: JointBorel T C (the standing measurability (2.3)), Assumption 2.2,
Assumption 2.3 with L, G.rank = min m n (Assumption 2.4), Assumption 2.5 with G, alpha, beta1,
beta2  ==>  0 < lamStar T L <= 1, and for every lam with lamStar <= lam <= 1 or 0 <= lam <= lamStar,
every PredForcing q, and any two ForcedSolutions (X1,Y1,Z1,U1), (X2,Y2,Z2,U2) of (4.1) at lam
with datum xi0 and forcing q: X and Y indistinguishable on [0,T], energy(Z1 - Z2) = 0 and
markedEnergy(U1 - U2) = 0.

Item by item against my locked reading:
 - lamStar: a function of (T, L) only, chosen before the setting and the coefficients -- matches
   "the threshold of Lemma 4.2, depending only on T, L and c_BDG" (c_BDG universal). As noted in my
   reading, since [lamStar,1] and [0,lamStar] cover [0,1], the conclusion is uniqueness at every
   lam in [0,1]; how lamStar is chosen does not change the strength. OK.
 - Hypotheses: (2.3) and Assumptions 2.2-2.5, the ones in force in subsection 4.4. Full rank as
   rank = min(m,n). Assumption 2.3 includes L >= 0; Assumption 2.5 includes the admissible-constant
   conditions (alpha, beta >= 0, alpha+beta1 > 0, beta1+beta2 > 0, m<n => beta1>0, n<m => alpha,
   beta2 > 0) and requires integrability of the pairings, which Assumption 2.3 supplies on the
   diagonal (harmless). Assumption 2.2 includes xi0 strongly F_0-measurable and in L^2. OK.
 - Forcing class: PredForcing -- q^b, q^sigma, q^f jointly and progressively measurable, finite
   energy, vanishing off [0,T]; q^h marked predictable with finite marked energy; q^g strongly
   F_T-measurable, L^2. The paper's class. OK.
 - Solution notion (ForcedSolution = WeakForcedSolution + E sup|X|^2, E sup|Y|^2 < infinity):
   X, Y adapted, cadlag (every path right-continuous, left limits), finite energy; Z, U predictable
   with finite energy, vanishing off [0,T]; the coefficient processes evaluated at Theta_s and
   lawP2 P Theta_s (the law of the time-s tuple; junk only at the null set of times where Theta_s is
   not L^2); h through a representative gamma required to equal h(s, Theta^-_s, ., Law Theta^-_s) in
   L^2(nu) for a.e. s, a.s. (constrained, not free); both identities of (4.1) a.s. for all t in [0,T]
   with the genuine L^2 Ito integral (cadlag version M) and the cadlag modification of the L^2
   compensated Poisson integral. This is "a solution of (4.1) in H". OK.
 - Conclusion: equality in H (X, Y indistinguishable; Z equal dt x dP-a.e.; U equal
   dt x dP x nu-a.e. on [0,T]). OK.
 - Non-vacuity: the hypotheses are witnessed by thm_cwp_hypotheses (Example 5.1(i), nu = delta_0,
   n = m = d = 1, T = 1, G = 1, alpha = beta1 = beta2 = L = 1), an instance the paper intends; and
   the solution notion is satisfiable there (sec45_proof_thm35 proves WP(1), whose existence part
   produces ForcedSolutions), so the uniqueness is not vacuously true.
Representation choices (harmless): coordinates; time over R with Z, U, forcings vanishing off
[0,T]; the law flow taken pointwise as lawP2 of Theta_s / Theta^-_s instead of a Borel
representative (they agree for a.e. s, and coefficients enter only through dt-integrals or the
a.e.-in-time representative gamma); h through a constrained representative gamma (the paper's
P x E-representative, (2.4)); predictable sigma-algebras without the time-0 slice; uniqueness in
H expressed as indistinguishability plus zero energies; the [lamStar,1] half is stated under
Assumption 2.2 too (the subsection's hypotheses; Lemma 4.3 would not need it).

Verdict: faithful with representation choices.

COVERAGE (claim A:sec4:uniqueness-along-homotopy; passage line 875 and its sentence, lines
875-878): the single clause states both assertions of the passage (uniqueness on [lamStar,1] and on
[0,lamStar]); "It remains to prove existence up to lam = 1" is not a mathematical assertion. It
states nothing the passage does not claim. The hypotheses are those in force in subsection 4.4
(the standing measurability (2.3) and Assumptions 2.2-2.5); strictly, the [lamStar,1] half needs
only 2.3-2.5 (Lemma 4.3) and the [0,lamStar] half only 2.2-2.3 (Lemma 4.2), so a statement split
by halves could carry fewer hypotheses, but the paragraph itself states none and sits under 2.2-2.5.

verdict.detail:
Representation choices, each harmless: (1) lamStar is an existentially chosen function of (T, L)
fixed before the setting and the coefficients, matching "the threshold of Lemma 4.2, depending
only on T, L and c_BDG"; since [lamStar,1] and [0,lamStar] cover [0,1] its choice does not affect
the strength; (2) processes as real coordinates, time over R with Z, U and the forcings vanishing
off [0,T]; (3) the law flow is lawP2 of the time-s tuple (and of the left-limit tuple for h)
instead of a Borel representative -- they agree for a.e. s, and coefficients enter only through
dt-integrals or the a.e.-in-time representative gamma, which is constrained to equal
h(s, Theta^-_s, ., mu^-_s) in L^2(nu) for a.e. s, a.s.; (4) predictable sigma-algebras generated by
(r,q]-rectangles (no time-0 slice, a null set of times); (5) equality in H written as
indistinguishability of X and Y on [0,T] and zero energy of Z1 - Z2 and U1 - U2; (6) the whole
statement is under (2.3) and Assumptions 2.2-2.5, the hypotheses in force in subsection 4.4,
witnessed by Example 5.1(i), where existence (WP(1)) shows the solution notion is satisfiable.
